title: Case Law: Use of Force
key_points: Graham v. Connor, 490 U.S. 386 (1989): force is judged by objective reasonableness from the view of a reasonable officer on the scene, considering severity of the crime, immediate threat, and active resistance or flight.

Tennessee v. Garner, 471 U.S. 1 (1985): deadly force may not be used to stop a fleeing suspect unless there is probable cause the suspect poses a significant threat of death or serious physical injury.
Scott v. Harris, 550 U.S. 372 (2007): reasonableness of ending a dangerous high-speed chase by force is judged on the facts, including the risk to the public.
officer_notes: NJ policy is stricter than these constitutional minimums; see the AG Use of Force Policy entry.
